records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Poisonous to Humans block (human-scoped, not a cat/dog-specific tag) rates this species Poison Severity: Low. Poison Symptoms: "Toxicity (usually low) to animals has occurred from Papaver plants. Since toxicity has occurred with similar plants, it is suggested this plant has toxicity too. All parts are poisonous including the juice." Poison Part is the full list: Bark, Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Roots, Seeds, Stems. Causes Contact Dermatitis is listed as No. Separately, NC State's Edibility note states: "Even though oriental poppies have some toxicity, condiments have been made out of seed heads when they are young" — an explicit partial-edibility statement (young seed heads only) alongside the toxicity rating, not a blanket not-edible claim. No admissible source (NC State or RHS) carries a cats/dogs-specific toxicity tag or scoping for this species; RHS's dedicated species page contains no toxicity statement at all.

normalizations: 2026-09-13: b82 landed from the post-audit records. Eight popular garden perennials: Woodland Sage, Lamb's Ear, Spiked Speedwell, Oriental Poppy, Anise Hyssop, Balloon Flower, Spotted Dead Nettle, Siberian Bugloss. All eight came back with toxic_to_pets null and none was manufactured: no admissible source names cats or dogs for any of them, and Oriental Poppy's only toxicity block is NC State's human-scoped 'Poisonous to Humans' block, kept in toxicity_detail with its scope stated. Auditor corrected wording used, with three rule-overrides: 'ranks nothing' / 'with no primary marked' / 'its first entry is not a primary name' were dropped from the Lamb's Ear, Siberian Bugloss and Spotted Dead Nettle name_notes (this catalog never attributes a ranking convention to NC State's alphabetized lists); the audit's '<dt>-label + values' substitutes for NC State's Common Name(s), Previously known as, Landscape Location and Soil Texture fields were trimmed to their values; and the audit's newline-stacked form of NC State's Lamium tag strip was replaced with the space-joined run the page actually renders (the tags are inline badges). The audit's title-string substitute for the Lamb's Ear alias sub-claim was replaced by the Donkey's Ears page's rendered heading, since a quote ending in NC State's title suffix is barred. Value changes: Oriental Poppy's outdoor_sun_exposure dropped part_shade (RHS Position lists Full sun only and NC State's prose directs full sun); Siberian Bugloss's soil_drainage restored as moderate, not moisture_retentive, and its water_regime left null; Lamb's Ear's is_houseplant landed false on NC State's Plant Type and hardiness-zone fields instead of null; Siberian bugloss title-cased to Siberian Bugloss. Declined: the audit's extended Missouri Botanical Garden Culture substitutes for Siberian Bugloss and Anise Hyssop -- plantfinder.mobot.org and www.missouribotanicalgarden.org both return ConnectError from this machine, so neither substitute could be ground-truthed; those two citations were dropped and the fields rested on verified NC State and RHS structured fields, with the decline disclosed in unknowns.
